key_observations: Stability fully resolved: fell_over_rate collapsed to 0.012 (≈0), perfect stability gate score. The doubled upright and quadrupled body_ang_vel weights achieved their primary objective.

locomotion_speed_mean of 0.077 m/s after 15k iterations is critically low — the robot is stable but nearly stationary. body_ang_vel_reward_weight at -0.2 (4× original) is the likely cause: it over-damps the natural torso oscillations required for dynamic forward walking.

Strong linear vs angular tracking asymmetry: track_linear_velocity=0.798 vs track_angular_velocity=1.579. The policy learned to rotate in place rather than translate — consistent with torso angular velocity being over-penalised.

gait_contact_cv_mean of 0.578 (>0.4 threshold) indicates irregular contact timing, and it worsened monotonically over the full run (0.333→0.584). This is downstream of the locomotion speed problem — fixing the gait dynamics should improve contact regularity.

mean_action_std of 0.587 after 15k iterations is above the healthy 0.2–0.4 endpoint (rule 4), suggesting the policy has not converged — it is still searching for a viable locomotion strategy under the current constraints.
All other metrics are within norms: landing_force_mean=41.8 N (healthy 30–90 N range), entropy decline is healthy (38% reduction, no collapse), symmetry costs are acceptable.
next_suggestion: Reduce body_ang_vel_reward_weight from -0.2 to -0.08 (keeping upright_reward_weight fixed at 2.0). This relaxes the over-constraint on torso angular dynamics that is suppressing forward locomotion, while staying above the original -0.05 to preserve the stability gains. Success criteria: locomotion_speed_mean rises above 0.3 m/s, track_linear_velocity recovers toward 1.0–1.2, fell_over_rate remains near zero, and gait_contact_cv_mean drops below 0.45.
